about.title: Palos Verdes Estates Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Palos Verdes Estates is a quiet coastal community, but people still get hurt while working here — landscapers on steep hillside properties, contractors doing home renovations, delivery drivers navigating Via Del Monte and Palos Verdes Drive West, and staff at local businesses. In most cases, California workers' compensation is your only path against your employer, regardless of who caused the accident. But when someone outside your employment relationship contributed to your injury — a subcontractor, a property owner, an equipment manufacturer, or another driver — you may also have a separate injury claim worth exploring. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we connect injured workers in Palos Verdes Estates with an independent attorney who can look at both the workers' comp side and any possible third-party claim, free of charge, so you understand your full set of options before deadlines pass.

whyChoose.title: Why Palos Verdes Estates Workers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: We Help Sort Out Two Different Systems
items.desc: Workers' compensation is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer no matter who was at fault, but a negligent third party can still support a separate claim. An independent attorney can help you figure out which path — or both — applies to your situation.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Matter
items.desc: California law generally requires you to notify your employer of a workplace injury within 30 days, so waiting can hurt your case. LawProactive can connect you quickly so an attorney can help you protect your options before time runs short.

items.title: Retaliation Protections Exist For A Reason
items.desc: It's illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting an injury or filing a workers' comp claim. If you're worried about your job, an independent attorney can explain your rights and help you move forward with more confidence.

items.question: I was hurt doing landscaping work on a private property in Palos Verdes Estates — can I file a claim?
items.answer: If you were an employee at the time, workers' compensation is typically the exclusive remedy against your employer, regardless of fault. However, if a property owner's hazardous condition or a third party's negligence contributed to your injury, you may have an additional claim worth reviewing. An independent attorney can help sort out which avenue applies to your specific job situation.

items.question: What if my injury happened while driving for work along Palos Verdes Drive West?
items.answer: Work-related vehicle collisions are usually covered under workers' compensation, but if another driver caused the crash, that driver's negligence could support a separate third-party claim with its own 2-year deadline. These two claims can move on separate tracks, so it helps to have someone review both.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for reporting a workplace injury?
items.answer: No, California law prohibits retaliation against employees who report an injury or file a workers' compensation claim. If you believe you've faced retaliation, an independent attorney can talk through what protections may apply to you and what your next steps could look like.
